summary: Piracicaba has a first-party municipal cadastral-information service and public geoprocessing viewer configured with an official WMS and a Lotes layer, but anonymous layer requests were empty and WMS capabilities timed out. The research packet is complete; no geometry sample or source admission is claimed.
queryAndRequestOutcomes: See city-6861-piracicaba.json requestsAndEndpointChecks. Separate English and Portuguese discovery queries were executed and their actual first-party URLs recorded. The municipal service page and current viewer/configuration were observed; anonymous layer-tree/map requests returned empty bodies and the WMS capabilities request timed out.
scopeLimits: The municipal page establishes a local Piracicaba cadastral custodian and describes property location and cadastral quadra/lote plans, but does not itself provide a machine-readable parcel geometry response.
The current viewer configuration establishes an official Lotes map route and WMS endpoint, but no native parcel identity, CRS, or feature geometry was returned.
The exact WUP point [-22.7253874086848, -47.653078712206] was preserved and was not shifted. Timeout/empty responses are not evidence of citywide absence.
No owner, address, contact, titleholder, personal, tax, account, or other unsafe fields were requested or retained.
No GeoJSON sample was retained because no unchanged native polygon response was obtained.

nativeIdentityReview.finding: No feature response exposed a native identity field; do not infer one from viewer/internal row numbering.

uncertainty: The official map backend may be transiently unavailable or may require a public profile/session not established in this attempt.
The configured WMS and Lotes theme are relevant official leads, not proof of a usable anonymous parcel API or citywide geometry coverage.
CRS, polygon validity, native identifiers, and bounded parcel response behavior remain unverified.
